transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-02 15:00 PT | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE), Sarah Lang (Aperture Head of ML), Tom Reese (CTO), Priya Patel (Security Lead)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Maya from Redwood — AE. Diego here from the infra team. We'll keep to 55 minutes.
[00:10] Sarah Lang: Hi Maya, Tom and Priya here from Aperture Robotics. Appreciate you taking the time.
[00:18] Diego Ruiz: quick intro — I'm Diego, solutions engineer; I'll dig into model and infra tradeoffs.
[00:25] Tom Reese: top level: we're selecting models for our procurement assistant. Needs to ingest long telemetry logs — roughly 20k-30k tokens per request today — and later we'll add multimodal inputs.
[00:40] Priya Patel: from security side: IP concerns, EU data residency, SSO/SAML for our org, and token-level audit logs.
[00:50] Maya Chen: got it. The main axes we'll cover: context length, multilingual (English/German/Japanese), tool-calling / function-calling for internal APIs, and deployment mode (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). Sound right?
[00:58] Sarah Lang: yes. We're currently on another managed provider; latency fluctuates and cost spikes when we send big contexts.
[01:10] Diego Ruiz: for long context you can choose models with native 32k windows like Redwood-Extended-32k or extended Llama-3 variants. Mistral-based models can work but sometimes need sliding-window approaches that can impact coherence.
[01:28] Tom Reese: quality is critical — hallucinations are a showstopper. We also need function-calling so the assistant can call internal endpoints. Does Redwood support tool-calling?
[01:38] Maya Chen: yes — hosted and Dedicated support function calling and tool invocations. Private can too but depends on your network egress policy; we can enable function-call hooks locally.
[01:48] Priya Patel: KMS requirements — we need BYOK with HSM for Private and preferably for Dedicated.
[01:56] Diego Ruiz: we do KMS integrations and can support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated. Our Console shows token-level traces and audit logs; we'll share examples.
[02:06] Sarah Lang: about context length: we need ~30k tokens. Any guidance on memory and quantization?
[02:14] Diego Ruiz: quantisation reduces memory but may slightly alter latency/throughput. Key thing is KV cache management for long-context. We sometimes recommend mixing prefix caching and chunking for very large docs. Note: customers spell quantization/quantisation differently in notes.
[02:30] Maya Chen: latency targets?
[02:33] Tom Reese: p95 under 600ms for small requests (≤1k tokens). For the 20-30k cases we can accept 2-3s but prefer under 2s. Cost sensitivity too.
[02:45] Diego Ruiz: Dedicated tends to give better unit economics at scale and predictable throughput; Hosted is easiest to start but costlier per token; Private gives isolation but adds setup time and ops.
[02:57] Sarah Lang: our legal team prefers Private, but if setup is long we may pilot on Dedicated. How long is Private onboarding?
[03:05] Diego Ruiz: varies — VPC-based Private can be 2-4 weeks; on-prem is usually 6-10 weeks. We can do a Dedicated pilot while standing up Private.
[03:18] Tom Reese: model comparisons: Llama-3, Mistral, Redwood variants — how do they fare for multilingual and long context?
[03:27] Diego Ruiz: Llama-3-70B-Chat-extended is strong at instruction following and multilingual; Redwood-Extended-32k is tuned for long coherence; Mistral is efficient and fast but sometimes less consistent on Japanese. We'll share evaluation spreadsheets showing per-language BLEU/ROUGE style metrics and human ratings.
[03:48] Priya Patel: function-calling control — can we restrict which tools certain roles can call? Need RBAC and per-route control.
[03:56] Maya Chen: yes — Console supports RBAC and route-level policies. You can restrict function-calling, set per-route model, and attach KMS keys.
[04:05] Sarah Lang: streaming support for large output?
[04:09] Diego Ruiz: yes streaming is supported. For long responses we recommend streaming plus prefix caching to reduce perceived latency.
[04:18] Tom Reese: any known limitations with tool-calling + long contexts? For example, extracting args from 25k of context.
[04:26] Diego Ruiz: extraction can add parse time; best practice is to synthesize a short context for the function-call step — pass minimal structured input to the tool-call layer. For multi-step orchestration split the job into shorter loops.
[04:40] Sarah Lang: multilingual benchmarks — do you have sample prompts for German/Japanese?
[04:45] Diego Ruiz: yes we'll share test corpora. German/Japanese performance is solid on Llama-3 variants and Redwood-Extended; Mistral sometimes needs language-specific finetuning.
[05:00] [05:00] (discussion continues on fine-grained evals and prompt design — Diego describes evaluation spreadsheets and metrics we typically run: pass@k, answer accuracy, hallucination rates)
[10:00] [10:00] (Diego walks through an example: 25k token doc, retrieval + chunking, and how prefix caching avoids repeated tokenization; mentions KV cache / K-V cache management and kernel selection differences on GPUs)
[15:00] [15:00] (Priya asks about pen testing and vulnerability cadence; Diego outlines SOC 2 compliance, quarterly vuln scanning, and optional customer-initiated testing for Private deployments)
[20:00] [20:00] (Maya reviews deployment choices: start with Hosted for quick POC, then Dedicated pilot for performance and cost, migrate to Private for final production if legal requires)
[25:00] [25:00] (Tom asks about model updates and version pinning; Maya explains rollouts, canary deploys, and automatic fallback policies for degraded variants)
[30:00] [30:00] (Cost discussion: Maya requests their monthly token projection; explains Dedicated reserved capacity math vs pay-as-you-go Hosted and provides back-of-envelope; agrees to send detailed pricing matrix)
[40:00] [40:00] (Technical deep dive: Diego discusses quantization tradeoffs, mixed-precision kernels, and how runtime selects optimized kernels by sequence length; notes some transcription glitches where "KV" was read as "K-V" in auto captions)
[50:00] [50:00] (Operational questions: audit logs, retention windows, SSO integration (SAML), and region locking for EU data residency; Diego confirms region-locking available for Private/Dedicated and will include contractual language)
[53:00] Maya Chen: quick recap — Diego will run the 25k benchmark on Redwood-Extended-32k and Llama-3-70B-extended in a Dedicated-like environment; Maya will send pricing, Dedicated sizing, and our security pack including SOC 2 and KMS/HSM integration docs; schedule follow-up next week for Dedicated sizing.
[54:10] Sarah Lang: if Private pilot timeline exceeds 6 weeks we'll start with Dedicated pilot; otherwise aim to go Private for production for data residency.
[54:35] Priya Patel: I'll email the compliance checklist and required retention policies by early next week.
[55:00] End of transcript.
